Open dungeon view after sending a team:
Egg that will hatch an Avian pet. Avian pets usually like to attract enemy attention, distracting them from the party.
Egg that will hatch a pet Construct. Constructs usually like to use magic to impair enemies and illuminate dark areas.
Egg that will hatch an Esoteric pet. Esoteric pets like to provide indirect bonuses, like granting enhanced learning, or finding more items.
Egg that will hatch a pet Insect. Insects usually like to attack enemies, and grant damage reduction.
Egg that will hatch a pet Reptile. Reptiles usually enhance the team offensive capabilities.
Egg that will hatch a Wild pet. Wild pets usually provide strategic support to the team, enhancing health management and offensive capabilities.
Egg that will hatch a Wooden pet. Wooden pets like to help the team stay alive, and are rarely keen for harming enemies.

Defying all the laws of basic biology, this monstrosity of connected tissues and nervous dead ends displays the strength of the many body it is made of. It feels no pain, so physical damage is less effective.

Purple fungus with white grains. Its flesh contains a paralyzing agent capable of halting respiratory functions in nearly every living creature. It moves slowly but with a rhythmic pattern, hinting at a form of sentience.
Left undisturbed for millennia, this living tree grew to a massive size. Its body is covered in spikes, a mighty weapon along with its size to keep the forest safe against harmful intruders.

The Arcane Assassins were a special operation group under direct command of the Seer, Kasimir, employed across the realms to take out targets that aimed to deteriorate the fragile peace among the various factions. They wield magical daggers gifted by the Seer, whose origin is a mystery.
"Extremely powerful and dangerous, Archmage is the title conferred upon the brightest mages in the city. They participate in the city's Higher Council, overseeing every major development."
A frail and feeble manifestation of an aspect of the Outer God. If the rituals were to be completed, it would bring dramatic and irreversible changes to life across the realms.

A terrifying breed of armored beasts that roam the Barren Wastelands. Due to their presence, this area was uninhabited since the beginning of recorder history, but fortunately they keep to their hunting grounds.
Extremely smart but evil creatures only found in the depth of the earth, beholder will smite their opponents with their eldritch powers.
An ancient warrior armed with twin mithril axes, his fury intensifies with every blow he endures, turning him into an unstoppable force as the battle rages on.
A corrupted bishop of an eldritch deity, wielding a grotesque form of magic gifted by their malevolent god. This power can heal extraordinary wounds but exacts a terrible price.
This humanoid of unknown origin, warped beyond recognition, has dwelled beneath these caverns for millennia. It toils ceaselessly to bring its long-forgotten god back into existence.
Wild boars are omnivorous animals commonly found in the forest. They can be hard to kill due to their thick skin.

"Only a handful of these flying fortresses are sent with the first wave to limit the risks associated with their loss, but as the campaign advances they slowly cover the target world's surface to assist the ground troops in the eradication of any form of life present."
The backbone of the Celestial Army. These fearless soldiers push through foreign worlds animated by unwavering loyalty, counting on a supernatural agility despite their large size.
Half men and half horses, these magical creatures are skilled hunters that used to live in harmony within the forest.
A sentient brain encased in nearly indestructible glass. It cannot move, but can manipulate the surrounding world in other ways.
A pale girl draped in a grimy white coat. Her modest appearance betrays the enormous knowledge she possesses.
A law enforcement unit operating in the Capital. They are not part of the Imperial Army, and their responsibility is to maintain order and catch criminals.
"One of the three cultist rebels. An extremely powerful mage, still couldn't manage to make the Primordial corruption-proof."

"A member of one of the many crusades from the eastern cities to eradicate the evil that has been abducting their citizen. They wander the halls aimlessly, having lost their ego over time to the magical influences. People from these lands seem to naturally display psyonic capabilities, and could present a formidable menace in large numbers."
A war hound employed by the Imperial Army, reanimated by the corruption after falling in battle. It feels no pain, so physical damage is less effective.

A capuchin colored monkey commonly found in the exotic Skull Island, home of the pirates. It has been trained to perform the lowliest duties of a pirate crew, like cleaning the decks and bringing the rum. It has also been trained in using the knife, and is a surprisingly strong adversary.
Powerful, benevolent desert spirit said to grand a wish to lucky travelers. After he became corrupt, he unleashes his wrath on every poor soul he crosses.
An incorporeal creature resembling a horse, with a single horn on its forehead.
This majestic, incorporeal dragon flies in hypnotic, looping patterns before striking with fierce power.
A mysterious, incorporeal figure seated behind an arcane instrument. Unfazed by the surrounding chaos, it is fully focused on its task.
An endless multitude of spectral, ravenous insects that tear their prey apart in seconds.
Elusive magical creature found in the southern woods. Its origin is unknown, but the travelers that spotted it before the corruption struck reported a timid but kind temperament.
These twisted, wolf-like creatures relentlessly hunt any creature that dares to approach the underground temple.
Electric charge flows through this slime body, threatening to shock anyone getting close enough.

"Once the most powerful man of the entire world, now twisted by corrupted rituals into a hideous mockery of his former self. He display the strength of a thousand men, and his expression, oddly enough, doesn't convey hate but only fear and confusion."
A warrior grotesquely altered through agonizing experiments, gifted with immense strength and a towering size.
Ancient guardians of the forest, these massive trees possess enormous strength.

"A fallen soldier of the Imperial Army, died during the last ditch effort of the Empire to stop the treacherous Seer.
It feels no pain, so physical damage is less effective."
This slime is engulfed by flames, but it seems okay with this condition.
A powerful figure in the Kaunian hierarchy, who gained terrible powers through the manipulation of its own body.
A sacred protector of the forest, who guarded it against external forces for millennia.
An extremely cold slime. Maintained the jelly-like texture despite the frozen coating, somehow.

"Gaussian Coil Security Station. Accelerates a giant metal projectile through a mysterious field, reaching incredible speeds and causing devastating damage upon impact. It's heavily armored, to sustain a prolonged assault."

For unknown reasons, sometimes undead are animated by a strong urge to feed on other dead bodies. These creatures often develop a more feral appearance, with longer teeth and sharper nails, and after some time they lose all of their similarity with human beings. It feels no pain, so physical damage is less effective.
Flies thanks to a magic powder that covers its wings. This powder is known to irritate the airways of many other creatures, including humans.
This kind of spider is usually found in much smaller sizes around the northern kingdoms. Left undisturbed for decades in the darkness of the Obsidian Mines, it reached the size of a grown man.
A huge tortoise weighting several tons, with a very hard shell covered in sharp spikes.
Old legends speak of the pet of a forest spirit in the form of a golden rabbit, but despite a few sighting its presence was never confirmed.
Large snake found in the southern regions that hunts by hurling saliva at its enemies at tremendous speed.
This nightmarish knight radiates an evil that defies imagination. Its own burning head, brandished as a morning star, grins malevolently as it is hurled at its foes.
The true form of the being once known as the Seer Kasimir. An eldritch being from another dimension, impervious to any form of mercy and loyal only to its God.
A powerful servant of the Black Serpent. Maintains the link through the Core, and will replace the Seer if its mission fail.
A powerful servant of the Black Serpent. Maintains the link through the Core, and will replace the Seer if its mission fail.
A powerful servant of the Black Serpent. Maintains the link through the Core, and will replace the Seer if its mission fail.

A mysterious creature that takes the form of extremely cold, inanimate rocks arranged in strange patterns. It appears to have complete mastery over the ice around, manipulating it offensively to dissuade attackers.

Slaves to the Celestial Goddess, abducted from the worlds she destroyed. Their bodies are modified to allow them to live through raging flames, and their mission is to cleanse the lands designated for the Cleansing.
A small, winged servant of the Wizards of Larox, summoned through magic and lacking any will of its own. It is typically used for simple tasks but can also assist in defending the city when needed.

A member of a special division of the Imperial Army appointed to the defense of the Imperial Palace and the many decentralized Imperial institutions. They are experts at protecting vulnerable targets, and can be formidable opponents even in their unhinged state.
Strategically crucial in every Imperial Army division, these highly trained mages conjure thunders above the enemy ranks, dealing substantial damage and disrupting their strategy.
"A citizen of the Empire Capital, who lived among luxury and wealth, never knowing any real hardship. The eye's appearance stole their sanity, and now they wander the streets in a feral state."
Merchants from distant lands often stopped by in the Golden City to sell exotic goods. They pose no greater danger than a normal citizen, but may carry more valuable resources.

A priest of one of the many places of worship in the city, used to offer guidance to the poor and the miserables. His strong faith granted him healing powers, that remained even after the loss of his sanity.

A powerful mage devoted to the forbidden arts who successfully completed the transformation into a lich. It remained well hidden into the catacombs for centuries, taking advantages of the large number of fallen soldiers to build a huge army. It feels no pain, so physical damage is less effective.

The eternal Seer who served the Emperor family for generations. Was considered an skilled advisor able to bring an age of peace and prosperity upon the Realms, he revealed his true intentions when he manifested the Great Serpent above the world.
The enormous shell of what was once a man. Wheter its current state is the result of external deception or its own hubris remains unknown.
This elegant, charismatic man conceals a dreadful curse behind his blood red eyes.

"One of the Celestial Army's high generals, sworn directly to the Celestial Goddess. His body has undergone extensive modifications to create the perfect warrior, and surviving this process is an exceptional achievement on its own. He is tasked with the purification of our world, and will stop at nothing to complete it."
"The result of a botched conjuring ritual. It possesses great strength, but it's existence is suffering."

Clad in a broken brass diving gear, barely producing any noise despite their limping gait, they can be rarely spotted in the obsidian mines. Their origins and purpose are unknown, but they appear to come from the lowest levels of the mine.

Armor crafted from a unique metal and brought to life through a blend of technology and magic. The city is teeming with these constructs, ever vigilant and prepared to fend off any potential invasion.

Not unlike a usual old, worn out chest filled with treasures (or spiderwebs), the Mimic true nature emerges when a poor soul tries to reach for its contents, often leaving more than they can retrieve. They are rarely found in the places under the control of the Skull Island pirates, and no one knows exactly what animates them.
Viscid, lined with suction cups, and with a tendency to sink random ships passing by. The only scarier thing than this tentacle is the creature it is attached to.
A soldier resurrected not by magic but through unknown technology, bound to carry out the commands of its masters.
"A colossal bone construct animated by forbidden magic. Bones are calcified together, therefore it can't move, but it's surface is harder than the hardest stone."
Lacking any magical power themselves, they work together to complete the Nexus of Larox and to discover new types of spells.

"Animated by unknown forces, this massive obsidian creature is impervious to any magic damage thanks to this element's properties. While hard to take down without a strategy, the massive size hinders it's offensive capabilities."

Flying organic-machine hybrid used to map terrain, find enemy locations and generally gathering information on the battlefield. Equipped with a small but powerful magic cannon that allows, through unknown technology, to replicate a destructive spell usually casted by mages through their rituals.

Lurking in the depths of the Obsidian Mines, this ancient horror made the original miners flee for their lives when it was mistakenly awaken. It strikes from the dark, leaving no chance to the unaware explorer.
Almost imperceptible to the naked eye, this extremely fast assassin will meet unprepared victims with a tremendous fate.
A massive bird resembling an eagle, with shimmering golden feathers and a gaze that burns like fire.

Only the most fearsome and ruthless pirates are given the command of a galleon. The pirate captains are formidable warriors, well versed in the art of diplomacy and rum drinking. They are in charge of some of the most difficult missions around the Realms.

The most common member of a pirate ship crew, Skull Island pirates are feared all over the realms. Trained in the use of the Cutlass, a traditional piratesque sword, they also have access to an exclusive technology capable of shooting iron projectiles with incredible force.
"Higher in the Skull Island pirate's hierarchy than the regular pirate, this seasoned lieutenant commands small crews in their plunders."

An ancient being of terrifying size, capable of devouring entire villages in a single bite. One of them is said to roam the ground below the Southern Grove, roaming in circle and unable to leave due to the rocky terrain surrounding the area.

"An ancient construct locked in the extensive halls below the Frostbite Peaks. Possesses a strength similar to that of a god, but since the ritual for it's creation involves mortal souls he is not impervious to the effects of the corruption."
A massive, flying living fossil from the dawn of this world. Remarkably strong, yet astonishingly agile in the air.
A large, imposing door. Attacks through a smaller Gaussian Coil fixed above, and the system that powers the room is reliant on its integrity.

"The last resort of the Sha'huri defense system. When invaders threaten the safety of their God, the defense system draws upon all its energy to conjure these fearsome warriors, capable of defeating large armies by themselves. Due to the immense energy cost these assaults should be short timed, albeit overwhelming."

"A sand warrior summoned by the legendary Sha'huri defense system, the last resort against external invaders to protect the core of their empire and their god. While not particularly strong by itself, they present a mortal threat by swarming the invaders in large numbers."
Birds of prey that scavenge on carrion. Not very dangerous alone, but ranged units are required to take them down.

"The legendary Guardian of the Sha'huri God, last line of defense between the invaders and the secret of the pyramid. His strength is legendary, and is the reason why the Sha'huri God remained unseen by anyone from outside the desert for thousands of years."

"The immortal God of the Sha'huri, writer of the original Prophecy, enemy of the Empire and eternal Prey of the Serpent. Not even It is immune from the effects of the corruption, therefore sealed itself in the inner chamber of the great pyramid."
"Skilled archer of the Sha'huri tribe, he offers ranged support for ground troops. They wield special bows able to disrupt enemy actions."
"Gifted with a fragment of their god's magic, they can manipulate the desert sand to encapsulate and crush their enemies."
"Fearsome warrior of the Sha'huri tribe, he executes the orders of the desert god."
The first physical, seemingly living being to appear in this world. Countless souls fused together as one, radiating an immense amount of energy.
A green, semi-transparent creature rarely spotted in the depth of the forest. From the few witnesses lucky enough to witness a Slime, they used to display an elusive behaviour before the corruption.
"Several times the size of a regular slime, their sovereign maintains the order in it's kingdom. It can wipe away an unruly underling with one gaze, and inflict a terrible fate on intruders."
A colossal demigod as tall as a mountain, birthed from the fiery depths of an active volcano. It moves slowly, crushing and incinerating everything in its path.
A majestic flying creature rarely spotted around the frostbite peaks. Unlike other draconids, it spits an ice tempest capable of sweeping away an unprepared army.
A mystic wielding a unique form of magic derived from stones unlike anything found on the surface. These stones allow them to command wild beasts with ease and grant them some healing powers.

"This vast, amorphous mass of organs and appendages dwells hundreds of meters beneath the Submerged Temple, orchestrating the Ritual. It is the most powerful of the Ancient's original, devoted apostles, it will stop at nothing to restore its master from its cosmic exile."
An immense, heavily armored dinosaur—slow-moving but with razor-sharp teeth. It can endure staggering amounts of damage before finally succumbing.

"To meet it's gaze is to peer into the unfathomable void of cosmic indifference. One glimpse at its figure unravels reason like a fragile thread. The terrified adventurers, however, feel like they already met this nightmare."
An extremely strong man slightly taller than average, who looks extremely calm. He looks out of place among the other prisoners. What secret is he hiding?
An enormous mechanical construct, an ever-shifting maze of angles and cogs, defying geometry and logic with every change in its configuration.
"One of the three cultist rebels. An extremely powerful mage, still couldn't manage to make the Primordial corruption-proof."
These living trees of medium dimensions used to be kind and caring towards wild creatures and travelers alike.

The very existence of these creatures baffled lore experts from around the Realms for centuries. They live in small sized tribes and conduct a primitive lifestyle based mainly on hunting. Their natural strength is unparalleled, and killing even one of them is a difficult feat.

"These trolls manifest some kind of healing power, different from the traditional white magic used by clerics but very effective in keeping their peers alive. Along with the troll's natural regenerative capabilities, killing a troll while they are alive is a difficult task."

"In the hierarchy of trolls, these individuals are assigned to the protection of the troll's hunting grounds from external forces. They are usually the strongest trolls of the pack, wielding a huge hammer as a weapon and striking fear into the hearts of explorers unlucky enough to have a close encounter with them"
"A young troll, not as dangerous as it's older peers, but already presents the defining features of their species, such as enhanced regeneration and a very hard skin."
An endless figure that entirely occupies the immense chamber. Housing this monstrosity must alone be the reason of the sheer size of this tower.
The corpse of a fallen archer, reanimated by the corruption. It feels no pain, so physical damage is less effective.
The corpse of a fallen infantry soldier, reanimated by the corruption. It feels no pain, so physical damage is less effective.

A reanimated high-rank General of the Imperial Army. During their life they were an exceptionally gifted soldier, deciding the outcome of key battles and leading hundreds of soldiers. It feels no pain, so physical damage is less effective.
This undead was likely a skilled commander, visibly stronger than the normal undead and clad in a spiked armor that hurts attackers. It feels no pain, so physical damage is less effective.
An extremely agile creature, it flies above its preys striking at the first opportunity, drawing their blood to restore its energy.
"A very unusual slime, with the texture of a starry night. It corrodes every surface in its trail, suggesting a conflict between its matter composition and the surrounding world's one."

A mysterious being from another world, brought into the fold as a result of Laroxians seeking unconventional alliances to bolster their ranks. The cost of its allegiance demands a sacrifice of untold proportions.
This incorporeal spirit is rarely spotted in large battlefields or cemeteries. There were never reports of them being aggressive towards the living. Completely ignores physical damage.
A gifted mage, made even more powerful through the endless knowledge of the Laroxians.
A wild wolf living in the forest. They can hunt alone or in packs.
Worm-like creatures with razor sharp teeth that dwell in the desert. They usually attack from below, and can draw energy from the flesh of their preys.

"You unlocked your first Epic Raid!
Epic Raids are like regular Raids, with the following differences:
• An Epic Raid has memory of your previous runs. If you win a fight once, you will not encounter it again.
• When you finish the Epic Raid and collect all loot, which will contain powerful unique items, it will disappear forever."
"Thin, greenish-brown plant that lives underwater. Its taste is salty and briny, and it's used mostly for exotic recipe typical of seaside settlements."
"A golden ethereal drink, extremely sweet and with a caloric intake which is off the charts. The way it's produced is unknown, but is sometimes carried from unknown lands by the traveling merchants."
Round and glossy, with skin colors ranging from red to yellow. It’s crisp, juicy, and sweet, with a slight tartness.
A golden, flaky crust surrounds a soft, spiced apple filling. It’s sweet and slightly tart, with cinnamon adding warmth to the juicy, tender apples.
It has a smooth, dark green skin with a creamy, buttery flesh inside. It’s mild and rich in fats, with a subtle, nutty flavor. Complements some of the most exotic, fish based recipes.
Yellow, sweet fruit found in tropical lands. Monkeys love them, even ones employed by the Skull Island fleet.
Small and round, deep blue or purple in color. Usually found in the colder mountain trails, it has a slightly tart flavors, and leaves a mildly floral aftertaste.
A fluffy, golden-brown pancake dotted with juicy blueberries. It’s soft and sweet, with bursts of tart blueberry flavor in each bite.

A thick, purple blend of blueberries and creamy ingredients. This recipe is not commonly found, as the few blueberries brought back from the troll ridden mountains were reserved for kings and princes.
"A soft, golden-brown crust gives way to a fluffy, airy interior. It's one of the most common foods in the Realms, enjoyed by paesants, soldiers and nobles alike."
A smooth, pale yellow spread that’s rich and creamy. It melts quickly, releasing a mild, slightly salty flavor with a hint of sweetness.
A grand, multi-layered cake with intricate decorations. Reserved for special occasions like the marriage of a royal, one of these cakes can feed a hundred guests.
"Solid milk derivative, ranging in color from yellow to orange. Its flavor is sharp and salty, and it's used in many delicious recipes."
Creamy, soft rice infused with melted cheese. It tastes mildly salty, with a smooth consistency.
A creamy, dense dessert with a smooth, rich texture. Tastes incredibly good, and pets love this.
Exotic food that only the upper class citizen of the Capital can usually acquire. Melts on the tongue releasing sweet, slightly bitter, and complex cocoa flavors with a creamy finish.
Deep brown liquid with a strong, earthy aroma. Nutritional content is close to zero, but allows for cooking delicious recipes.
Golden and slightly crispy chocolate sweet with a soft, chewy center. A refined food destined to the breakfast of nobles, ambassadors and rich merchants.
Halved boiled eggs with a yolk filling. The filling is extremely spicy, so this dish is not for every palate.
Massive, meaty ribs with a thick, tender texture. Packed with protein, they make a hearty meal, but the ancient beasts they come from are incredibly challenging to hunt.
A smooth, oval shell encasing a firm white and a bright yellow yolk. When cooked, it becomes either soft and creamy or firm, with a mild, rich taste.
Complemented with pineapple pieces, this fruit salad is juicy, sweet, and tangy, offering a burst of tropical flavors.
A vibrant pink-orange fish with a firm, yet tender meat. Fished in the waters just above Blackwater Port, its taste is rich, buttery, and slightly sweet, with a moist, flaky texture when cooked.
Deep red, firm flesh that’s meaty and dense. Valuable fish rarely found in the high seas, it has a clean, mild flavor with a slight hint of salt.
A cold, misty soup with an icy, translucent appearance. The broth helps to make the Wyvern meat more tender, but chewing it is still a daunting task for many.
A colorful mix of fresh, juicy fruits, sweet and with a soft bite and a vibrant, refreshing flavor.
A soft, fluffy ring of dough coated in a glossy, sugary glaze. Popular among the north-eastern settlers, the exact recipe is not known.
"An experimental way of serving a cold , sweet flavoured cream. It's a rare speciality only a few select food lovers ever had a chance to taste."
A small bag of dry kernels with various shapes and colors. They have a slightly chewy texture when cooked and a neutral, earthy flavor.
Golden, crispy bread surrounds melted, gooey cheese. The sandwich is warm and rich, with a satisfying crunch and a creamy, salty interior.

The epitome of experimental, nouvelle cuisine. A taco using the hard Wyvern meat as filling, completed with the hottest sauce in the realms. A unique experience for sure, but definitely not for everyone.

A dark, revolting soup with an eye floating in it. You can’t tell if the eye fell in by accident or if it’s part of the recipe. It looks vile, and there’s only one way to find out if it will kill you.
Long and cylindrical with pale green and white layers. Its flavor is mildly sweet, like a delicate cross between onions and garlic, with a crisp, firm texture.
Smooth, creamy, and white with a rich, buttery texture. It has a mild, slightly sweet taste and a velvety consistency that melts easily.
A massive, towering burger with layers of juicy meat, melted cheese, crisp lettuce, and savory sauces. Not very healthy, but extremely caloric.
"A thick, juicy cut of meat complete with a bone. It's the cheap, nutritious base for most meat based dishes."
A golden, flaky pastry crust surrounds a savory filling of tender meat. It’s warm, hearty, and packed with robust, meaty flavors.
A warm, hearty mixture of slow-cooked ingredients. Tender chunks of meat float along with vegetables in the broth.
Soft and spongy with an earthy, mild flavor. Rarely found in the southern forests, where the damp climate sometimes allows for their growth.
White and smooth with a creamy consistency. It’s mild, slightly sweet, and soothing. Can be turned into many derivatives, used in a large amount of recipes.
A fluffy, golden omelette filled with tender mushrooms. It’s soft and savory, with a rich flavor and a slightly creamy texture.
Creamy rice with tender Meaty Mushrooms. A very esteemed dish, given the difficulty of importing this kind of mushrooms in the northern cities even prior to the corruption.
A warm, earthy dish filled with tender mushrooms. The broth is thick and flavorful, with a slightly spongy texture.
Long spaghetti derived from grains, a common food found in many towns and villages. It provides a satisfying, slightly chewy texture and can be perfected with sauce.
Long spaghetti derived from grains, a common food found in many towns and villages, coated in a bright red sauce.
With a smooth yellow skin, their flesh is soft, juicy, and sweet with a grainy texture that will melt in the mouth.
A buttery, golden crust holds a soft, sweet pear filling. The pears are tender and juicy, with a delicate sweetness and subtle spiced aroma.
A spiky, golden-brown exterior hides bright yellow flesh. It’s juicy, tangy, and sweet with an exotic, refreshing flavor.
A starchy, oblong vegetable with a brown skin, considered a staple in the common villager diet. Its inside is soft, fluffy, and mildly earthy when cooked.
"Smooth, creamy mashed potatoes with a buttery flavor. It's a simple dish enjoyed by every social class in the Realms."
Vibrantly orange with smooth, firm flesh. They grow only in the upper caverns below the Gates of Hell, thriving in the Nexus artificial light.
A small, wrinkled red pepper with a sinister appearance. Its taste is fiery and incredibly spicy, leaving a sharp, lingering heat on the tongue.
"A fiery, bright red sauce with an intense, lingering heat. It’s incredibly spicy, not very nutritious by itself and it's highly recommended to not eat this alone."

Tiny, white smooth grains that, when cooked, present a neutral taste and a soft texture. Often used as the main supply for soldiers embarked in long expeditions, as it is easy to conserve for long times.
A simple mix of crisp leeks and colorful tomatoes. It’s light, crunchy, and refreshing, but not one of the most nutritious dishes.
A slice of fresh, bright orange salmon atop a small bed of rice wrapped in seaweed. A staple dish in the diet of sailors, pirates and sea merchants.
"A sushi roll with soft rice, avocado and fresh salmon. Hard to make since ingredients must be imported from very distant areas, it's considered a delicacy even in the richest cities."
"Small, white granules or crystals with a sharp, savory taste. While it's not advised to consume salt alone, it can enhance most recipes. It is also widely used to conserve foods."
A smooth, liquid or semi-liquid mixture derived from tomatoes, leek and a bit of salt. It adds moisture, richness, and depth to dishes.
Colorful and aromatic, while not able to sate hunger by themselves, they can be added to a lot of recipes to emphasize their taste and appearance.
A slow-cooked, tender steak with a deep brown exterior. It’s rich and flavorful, with a slightly smoky taste.
A warm, hearty mixture of slow-cooked ingredients. It’s thick and comforting, with tender chunks of vegetables suspended in broth.
Bright red, heart-shaped berries with tiny seeds on the outside, known to grow in the southern forests because of the warmer climate. It’s juicy and sweet, with a slightly tart edge.
A light, fluffy pancake topped or filled with sweet strawberries imported from the southern forests. It’s soft and slightly sweet, with a fresh, juicy pop from the strawberries.
A pink, creamy drink bursting with sweet, juicy strawberries. A common, albeit expensive recipe before the corruption struck, when the southern forests creatures were shy and peaceful.
Tender meat chunks coated in a glossy, reddish sauce and pineapple pieces. The flavor is a perfect balance of tangy sweetness and a mild sour kick.
A crunchy bread slice filled with meat, cheese, and sauces. It’s savory and nutritious, with a mix of different textures.
"A layered dessert with creamy mascarpone and espresso-soaked cookies. It has a smooth and sweet taste, and it's extremely nutritious."
Round and smooth, with a bright yellow color. Its flesh is juicy and slightly sweet with a tart, refreshing flavor and soft seeds inside.
Deep red tuna on rice, firm yet tender, wrapped in seaweed. A delicacy sometimes found in the diet of pirates and wealthy sea merchants.
"A sushi roll made with red tuna, avocado and rice. Hard to make since ingredients must be imported from very distant areas, it's considered a delicacy even in the richest cities."
Slightly colored liquid with a sharp, pungent aroma. It delivers a sour, tangy taste that is perfectly suited for some of the more elaborate dishes.

Few people manage to take down a Wyvern, and even fewer manage to bite through its extremely hard meat. The taste is described as very intense, and the meat as extremely nutritious, with a single bite able to sustain a soldier for a day.
Creamy and smooth milk derivative. White in color, it’s tangy and slightly sour, with a rich, thick consistency that varies from silky to dense.
Are you sure that you want to buy another try for %d gems?
You can see the items you put for sale here. After some time, visiting travelers will purchase them.
Adventurers rest here. By expanding your quarters, you will be able to recruit more adventurers.
You can house your Pets in the Shelter. You will be able to house more pets as you expand its capacity.
- Long press to mark a pet for auto feeding

"Pets can be hatched from Eggs, which are randomly dropped by several enemies.
You can level up pets giving them Food. Leveling up, they will unlock new abilities, and improve the strength of their current ones.
Autofeed allows to select pets that will automatically feed on any food item found, the moment it is collected."
Short tap to view, long press to sell
Travelers from distant settlements may stop here for a drink from time to time. If you like any of them, recruit them into your guild!

"When the tavern is full, the older guests will leave to make room for new ones.
If you see an interesting unit but you prefer to recruit it later, you can freeze the current list by toggling the \"lock\" icon."
This is the place where your most skilled blacksmiths, tailors and alchemists create new items.

"The minimum and maximum damage inflicted with every basic attack.
%s"
Damage of Bows scales with Dexterity
Damage of Daggers scales with Constitution + Dexterity
The minimum and maximum damage inflicted with every basic attack.
Damage of Staffs scales with Intelligence
Damage of Swords scales with Constitution
Affect the damage of Swords and Daggers. After damage is reduced by Defense or Magic Defense, it is further reduced by one for every 8 points of Constitution.
Chance to counterattack with a basic attack when hit by a melee strike.
Percentage increase in damage dealt for every point of darkness in the current area.
Reduction to the level of darkness in the current area.
Health lost at the start of every turn.
Percent reduction to physical damage received
"Affect the damage of Bows and Daggers. Physical attacks have 0.4% critical chance per point, up to 40%. Affect the chance to dodge physical attacks."
Bonus dodge chance added to the base one rolled comparing the relevant statistic.
Percentage of experience gained after defeating an enemy.
When the experience bar is full, the adventurer gains a level. When the adventurers faints, experience towards the next level is lost.
Percentage of health restored by healers.
When the HP reaches 0, the adventurer faints. Once the whole team is fainted, the party will need a while to resume the exploration.
"Affect the damage of Staffs and mana regeneration. Magic attacks have 0.4% critical chance per point, up to 40%. Affect the chance to dodge magical attacks."
When an adventurer reaches its maximum level, they can be promoted to a stronger unit.
Percentage of damage inflicted that is converted to health for the attacker.
Percent reduction to magical damage received
When the mana reaches %d, the adventurer will cast its Active Skill. The mana gain formula is [10 + (Intelligence / 10)] per turn.
For every potion drank, increase Dodge Chance by 1%.
For every potion drank, increase Constitution by 1.
For every potion drank, increase damage dealt per point of darkness by 0.1%
For every potion drank, increase Defense by 1.
For every potion drank, increase Dexterity by 1.
For every potion drank, increase maximum HP by 5.
For every potion drank, increase Status Immunity by 1.
For every potion drank, increase Intelligence by 1.
For every potion drank, increase Magic Defense by 1.
For every potion drank, increase Critical Hit chance by 1%.
For every potion drank, increase Critical Hit damage by 2%.
Health regenerated at the start of every turn.
Physical/Magical damage dealt back to melee attackers.
Chance to avoid being inflicted a negative Status Effect.
The weight of this unit when a target is rolled among a pool of units.
A piece of fabric of unknown origin, worn by the members of a cult that wishes for the return of the Ancient.
An artificial mechanism that can control an organic brain, amplifying its capabilities enough to manipulate the physical world that surrounds it.
Viscous potion that can enhance some base materials with additional, terrifying properties.
A black Iron ingot blessed with eldritch properties from the depth of the abyss.
Large seashell found in the north-western seas. Mostly used as decoration, possesses some interesting properties.
Flammable liquid used to make flight possible for the heavy flying ships of the Celestial Army.
The mysterious substance responsible of infusing life into the titans roaming the cultists lair. The origin seems organic.
A partitularly long tooth, once belonging to the leader of a pack of wolves.
Blood drawn from Lazarus, the first vampire.
Scale covered hide of a giant, archaic beast living at the center of the world.
An incredibly durable yet lightweight membrane, taken from the wing of a creature believed to have gone extinct millions of years ago.
A hardened, very old seed that seems to possess magical properties.
Metal ingot smelted from pieces of Living Metal.
Pieces of an unknown metal. They move erratically when left alone, and pulsate with an eerie light.
"A chunk of a giant, nightmarish monster that surpasses a mortal's wildest fantasy. You are not sure of its utility."
A bag of irritant powder that Giant Moth wings are covered in. It allows for a more aerodynamic flight, but irritates the airways of most other living beings.
The sharp and resilient claw of a Banshee
Twisted, black horn of a Banshee
Hard scale making up the skin of a Banshee
Frontal tooth of a Vampire Bat. Sometimes used as alchemic ingredient.
The resilient wing of a Vampire Bat.
The pelt of a wild animals, usually refined to make Leather.
The skin of a horrible monster preying in the dark.
"Extremely resistant metal alloy. It's formula is jealously guarded by the pirate blacksmiths."
Scraps of the famed metal, ready to be fused into an ingot.
A dense, sticky black substance. It is believed to be a byproduct of the soul-stealing process from the eldritch gods.
A well preserved tusk from a wild boar.
Fragments of a bone once belonging to a valiant soldier.
A powerful Djinn spirit trapped in a bottle.
An ingot made from recovered scraps.
Hard metal with an impossibly high fusion point. Must be some kind of alloy made with unknown ingredients.
Surprisingly light ring of unknown metal, seems to possess some magical properties.
Light but very resistant chain that seems to reflect part of the incoming force, magical or not.
"A coal chunk vaguely resembling the shape of a heart, still weakly beating despite its condition, and the fact that it has been extracted from the owner's chest."
A clear blue concoction able to restore the original properties of items degraded due to the corruption.
A versatile textile usually employed in the production of robes or cloaks.
"Unrefined mass of Giant Spider's cobwebs. Can be refined into an unbreakable textile."
"A purse full of coins of various denominations. Worth it's weight in silver."
Glass orb reinforced by magic, needed to contain powerful but dangerous artifacts.
An ingot made of copper. Can be smelted in any shape to produce all kinds of equipment.
A malleable metal with a distinctive reddish-brown hue.
Exotic kind of leather that comes from processed Monkey Hide.
The fur of the elusive Golden Rabbit.
A thick potion displaying a vivid red color.
The woven seal of the Crusaders of the Eastern Kingdom. A symbol of hope for their people, heralding light in their darkest moments.
An extremely light chunk of silver that glows with an eerie light.
A piece of Exotic Velvet blessed with eldritch properties from the depth of the abyss.
A very hard gem that appears to be impossible to scratch. Only a handful of these have ever been found on the surface, making it an ideal gift for powerful kings or emperors.
Hide fetched from a dangerous, colossal dream creature. Due to its origin it is very versatile, but less resistant.
The first stage of development of an insect materialized from a dream.
The thick mane of a Dreamwrought Beast.
Extremely flexible cloth woven from a dream like thread. Due to its origin it is very versatile, but less resistant.
Very malleable metal materialized from a dream by an expert blacksmith. Due to its origin it is very versatile, but less resistant.
A sheath of a weird material that could be either natural or artificial.
The Seal of the Outer God, worn by his priests to show their unwavering faith.
A fragment of a larger tapestry, it can be combined with other pieces to reveal the complete picture.
One of the tendrils of a Beholder. You can feel its powerful magic still flowing into the appendage.
Arcane catalyst used to balance the properties of powerful, unstable elements.
Very difficult to brew even for the most skilled alchemists, made from ingredients of legendary rarity, this elixir acts as a neutral glue for substances that would otherwise reject each other.
Magic concoction that briefly boosts the ability of a student to learn new concepts.
An unusually long bone, probably coming from a hind leg of a war hound.
An extremely rare wood found in a minority of trees in the Southern Lands. Seems to keep sprouting new branches even when chopped off the original tree.
Precious green gemstone, widely employed in the field of jewelry.
Pitch black potion distilled from the Black Ooze. When purified through additional steps, it can manifest unique properties.
Alchemic powder enriched to display new magical properties. Only this powder is pure enough to be merged with the Primordial, increasing its strength.
Very smooth and prestigious textile imported by pirates from distant lands.
"Seeing its dimensions makes you wonder what kind of monsters lurk in the ocean's depth. Powerful and very rare alchemic ingredient."
"The eyes of the first general of the Sha'huri Army. A unique battle trophy."
A very light feather with a variety of uses.
Arcane catalyst used to balance the properties of powerful, unstable elements.
An oil obtained through unknown means that allow anything covered in it to be immune to fire.
A piece of an incredibly powerful being, that somehow crossed the threshold between the mortal world and something else.
A magic textile enchanted by unknown rituals. Grants the wearer a reduction in its weight.
An organic mass of nerves and tendrils, shaped to have specific optic properties.
An extremely sharp crystal displaying minor magical properties. Despite its nature, it never melts.
The magic pebble around which an Ice Elemental can form.
An ingot of a peculiar type of metal that mixes the properties of iron and ice.
A raw piece of very strong and cold metal. Can be smelted into ingots.
"The egg of a Snow Wyvern. It's unique properties seem to increase the danger cold weather poses to those around it."
A scale of the fearsome Snow Wyvern. Always a few degrees lower than room temperature.
"Ghostwood replacement for a lost leg, a common occurrence in the pirate's world."
Board of Ghostwood ready to be employed for the creation of various equipments.
A moth wing of unusual dimensions, possesses greater elasticity than its smaller counterparts.
A piece of an extremely hard shell.
A mysterious reagent gifted by a god of light.
Sand heated to form transparent, smooth surface.
A precious metal widely employed in the production of high-grade military equipment for the Imperial Army.
Scraps of gold retrieved from broken equipment. Can be smelted into ingot.
Green, transparent jelly that makes up the body of Slimes.
The heart of a being predating existence itself. An expression of hatred unmatched by anything else.

Water blessed with a secret ritual by a bishop of the capital. Can be used to remove curses from items or living creatures, but due to the length of the rituals involved in its production only the most wealthy individuals can afford it.
Arcane catalyst used to balance the properties of powerful, unstable elements.
A thin thread of ice-like textile, likely made with a technique only known to the Trolls.
Blood carrying the mysterious infection that can turn regular undead into ghouls. Can be used as alchemic ingredient.

Mysterious mineral forged by the hottest fire, remarkably resistant yet light as a feather. Oddly cold at touch, allows to forge items with impossible aerodynamics, not reproducible with any other means.
An oil that can be applied to certain armors or garments, able to boost the learning speed of those who wear it.
A durable and resistant metal, usually employed to craft battle armaments.
Smooth, pale white material derived from tusks of animals.
Rare metal from the eastern lands. Displays some unique properties, likely coming from the psyonic ability of the people who smelted it.
"Thick and hard fabric displaying properties more close to those found in metal. Doesn't display any magical property, but will do an excellent job in protecting its owner."
Cold at touch, this peculiar gem reflects light with a flame-like shimmer. Seems to draw the curiosity of the nearby wildlife.
An intact eye of a slain Beholder. Can be used as a perfectly focused magic lens.
An incredibly resistant but light fabric, enchanted with a variety of spells to enhance its properties.
A resistant but light material, usually employed in the making of armors or armor paddings.
The sap from a living tree.
A long, resistant vine ripped from an ancient tree that moves on its own volition.
A very long and sharp fang taken from a wild Spitfang.
Looks like regular sand at first glance, but displays peculiar shapeshifting properties.
A single page of some old book.
A legendary alloy, unbreakable by traditional means. Its creation remains a guarded secret of the dwellers of the Forgotten Lands.
The hide of a Capuchin Monkey, a small primate usually kept as pet and assistant by some Skull Island pirates.
Extremely thick skin from a creature mutated through horrifying experiments. Hard to adapt to the human body, but impenetrable with conventional weapons.
The viscid limb taken from a deep sea monster.
A simple brass cog. No one knoes its exact function, or can explain the immense power it contains.
High end leather sought after in all the Realms. Retrieving this material is so dangerous that only few people have ever owned it.
Dark, reflective stone famous for its durability, and sharpness when broken into pieces.
An orb of otherworldly matter, stirring upon itself in an endless dance.
Unbreakable metal from another world. Sacrifices malleability to increase its resistance.
Pieces of an unbreakable metal that can be melted into ingots.
Perfectly round and with a smooth surface. Very prized material for jewelers.
Unstable core that instantly freezes everything around it.
Stabilized Permafrost Core, can be used to craft powerful items.
A feather plucked from the mythical Phoenix.
Fragment of a powerful artifact. Has something to do with death-altering magic.
A base ingredient used in the production of textiles.
The flesh of a mushroom that lives deep underground. It contains a strange poison with a paralyzing effect, and requires careful handling.
A strange amalgam of ingredients from the depths of the Forgotten Lands, seamlessly fused together and exhibiting unique catalytic properties.
The enormous scale making up the armor of a colossal Wurm roaming below the Southern Grove.
The essence of a primordial being, commonly used as alchemic ingredient.
Stabilized essence displaying a variety of colors, elementally neutral but radiating pure arcane energy.
Giant claw of a flying monster previously thought to be extinct.
Hard, crystalline mineral found rarely in the deserts and prized for its beauty.
A powerful, magical device that can store an immense amount of energy. Serves as an engine for Laroxian constructs.
"A peculiar recurve blade. Unusable in the current state as it's handle is missing."
Peculiar wood from the far east, rarely found in trading points thanks to traveling merchants. Displays a characteristic red shade.
Deep red gemstone with a rich allure, and used to craft a wide range of jewels
Rune carefully engraved with great mastery into a simple rock, capable of increasing the power of a wizard by orders of magnitude.
A stone made of sand solidified into a stone-like block.
An unknown device made of flesh, metal and stone. Seems capable to detect movement without relying on light.
Gift from an ancient divine force to its worshippers. Only a few exemplars are known to exist, and their strength and quality is legendary.
Pieces of metal that usually comes from broken battle gear. Can be smelted into ingots and recycled.
Magic seal of Claris, the rebel Cultist.
A stone slab from one of the titans created in secret with a cursed ritual.
When a living being touches this gem, whatever their nature is, they are instantly drawn to darkness.
With a bright purple color, items can be infused to provide bonuses in dark areas.
"The bow frame used to make the renowned Sha'huri bows."
"A rib ripped from an undead soldier. It's well conserved and very sharp."
Luxurious, smooth fabric prized for its softness and sheen. Used to craft superior light clothing.
Delicate fiber used to weave the fabric of the same name.
A powerful catalyst used to clear the arcane properties of powerful artifacts that may be cursed, or magically bound to another entity.
Condensed fragment of the multitude of souls, crystallized inside the creature they inhabited.
Otherworldly textile made with a glowing thread. Clearly not crafted by human hands.
Skin of a creature conjured through a spell, persisting in this world after its defeat.
Leather made from the skin of a creature summoned through magical means.
Leg of a Giant Spider. Can be used as alchemic ingredient.
"Made from an almost indestructible thread, this light material offers protection with minimal hindrance to one's movements."
A magic candle of mysterious origin. It never burns out, and cannot be extinguished with any known mean.
Light and resilient scale making up the skin of a Spitfang.
A fragment of a distant star, containing an immense amount of power.
Unstable core displaying an extremely strong electric field.
Stabilized Static Core, can be used to craft powerful items.
Unstable core burning with the power of a small sun.
Stabilized Sunfire Core, can be used to craft powerful items.
A small wire capable of conducting electric and thermal energy extremely well.
The decomposed hide of an undead war beast.
Giant tooth of a voracious creature found in the depth of the world.
Once infected blood drawn from a fearsome ghoul, it has been purified by a powerful reagent. Unlike the base ingredient, it displays powerful healing properties.
A very sharp thorn broken off a Giant Tortoise shell.
Hard as a stone but light as regular leather. Used to craft superior quality equipment.
All living beings are naturally repelled by its smell. The antithesis of all that is good, conveniently condensed in liquid form.

A gem that vibrates in its own magical frequency. These are the building blocks of the immense Laroxian Nexus, and will one day be correctly attuned and integrated into its design to amplify its power.
A staple tool in the bag of the arcane engineer. Allows workers without the gift of magic to manually operate across the veil that separates the physical world from the Arcane Flow.
An extraordinarily powerful magical artifact, capable of overcoming any opposing magical force. It is the only known way to directly interact with the Nexus Core.
Unstable core surrounded by a void area where no regular matter can exist.
Permeated with an ancient, despicable magic, in the right hands this simple cloth doll could inflict unimaginable suffering to an unaware victim.
Hard leather belt characterizing the outfit of the wardens of the Golden City.
"An intact skull of a renowned soldier, once leading it's ranks against the enemy."
Something is really wrong with this tooth…
A white blob taken from the body of a one of a kind slime deity.
እንደ ላይ እንደ ታች። አሥርቱ ገሃነሞች እንደገና ተከፍተው ይሆናል፣ በመሠዊያችንም እንደ ሁሉም ይበላሉ።
Very light and elastic textile made from the wings of moths.
Despite being a very thin cloth, it isolates almost perfectly from the external cold.
Very sturdy wood from the only tree that can grow in sub-zero temperatures, the Winter Tree.
Just a simple piece of wood.
Blood drawn from a Wurm. Can be used as alchemic ingredient.
Very hard keratin scales covering the body of the desert Wurms. Can be used as plates to reinforce equipment.
%s is resurrected by the Amulet of Resurrection
From a nearby wall, reanimated bodies crawl towards the expedition
A nearby wooden door is shattered into a thousand splinters by a towering presence.
In front of them, an undead clad in a golden armor orders its followers into the battle. A curious display of sentience for an undead, the team notes.
From the darkness, the monsters start running at the adventurers.
A second wave of undead leaves the team no respite.
Inside the crypt, a decrepit skeleton holding a metal scepter lets out a frightening scream.

"The team crosses the dark entrance to the ancient Catacombs of the Eternal battlefield. This is an ancient place where, after the agreement of the year fourteen of the eternal war, both factions can give their fallen high-ranking fighters a worthy burial. Strangely enough, instead of finding a quiet place, horrible sounds are coming from the lower levels…"
"Without its master's magic to hold the pieces together, the Necrolith crumbles to dust."
The adventurers take the first step beyond the open door.
The voice speaks again, this time a bit clearer. It says \"Come forth, my children. Come join my ranks.\"
The door is unlocked, and reveals a circular crypt.
"The room is now empty, and the screams have stopped. There isn't really a way to kill a lich, but it should stay quiet for a while. The team turns back and reaches for the surface."
Piles of skulls and bones are piled up on the sides, covering the walls of the corridor.
The air becomes more chilling, the corridor darker. The noises from below are almost unbearable.
The corridor ceiling gets a bit lower.
The group resumes their expedition, taking a flight of stairs down to the lower levels.
The stairs end, and the corridor opens into a large, dark hall.
A voice of unknown origin, as dry as these putrid walls, echoes in the hall. It is not loud enough to understand.
In the center of the circular hall, a pillar made of bones holds up the tall ceiling.
At the end of the now empty hall, an adorned iron door blocks the path.
The team steps into an unavoidable fight.
In the open field, the team is spotted from far away.
Just in time, the adventurers turn around to find enemies charging at them.
After a strenuous run, the expedition realizes it must face the chasing threat.
From behind a large fire burning in the plain, something attacks the expedition.

A desolate land stretches as far as the eye can see. These are the hunting grounds of the Banshees, ruthless armored beasts known for their solitary nature. However, something else is going on: constructs resembling flying eyes roam the skies, while the horizon looks like a sea of flames.
In the ground, in an abandoned Banshee burrow, lies a poorly concealed alien weapon. The team is about to step on the tripwire.
"Far away, a Banshee crawls out of the ground and leaps to an unsuspecting invader trying to burn some remains. It's over before he even notices the attacker."
Fires are burning all around the team, making the air almost unbreathable.
A large celestial platoon is marching to the north. The team hides behind a nearby rock, waiting for them to pass.
A wounded Banshee digs a hole in the ground at surprising speed and disappears inside it.
"A flying ship is scanning the ground for living targets. You hope it didn't locate the expedition."
A huge golden ship, clearly not from this world, appears in the sky out of thin air. Tens of celestials jump down several meters on an unsuspecting Banshee.
On your left, a group of celestials are pouring an unknown liquid inside one of the holes on the ground.
The team proceeds with caution, surrounded by the sounds of the ongoing battle.
On the ground are still visible the remains of a recent skirmish.
A large group of flying eyes floating above suddenly divides, each racing in a different direction.
Hostile entities appear from behind a nearby lowered sail
A glass bottle cracks nearby. Immediately after, something attack you.
Distracted by the rustling of the waves, you realize almost too late you are being followed.
From below the docks, something emerges. It wants your heads.
The cracking of the wood planks below alerts you of the incoming attack.

Few people who enter Blackwater Port uninvited get to leave on their feet. Controlled by the fearsome pirates of the nearby Skull Island, because of their agreements with the Empire this was the central commercial hub of the region. It is said that the place was already cursed before the corruption struck.
"It's been a while since you haven't ran into a soul… what could be scaring these ruthless pirates?"
You notice a huge, dark spot just below the surface. What kind of horror lies under the sea?
The unknown mass goes back to the dark ocean depths.
"A small round object is floating in the water. With some difficulty, the team manages to retrieve an Eye of the Abyss. The monster is far from dead, but it's surely hurt."
A scared capuchin monkey emerges from beyond some crates. How long was it hiding there? It hands you a polished oyster pearl, and runs to the woods outside the port.
A tripwire suddenly snaps, triggering nearby flintlock guns aimed at the team.
When a team member steps on a hidden pressure plate, a huge anchors falls from above.
A pile of gold is sitting in front of the adventurers. As soon as they touch it, the curse activates and it turns into a sticky, corrosive substance.
A suspended net is released onto the adventurers, ensnaring them. The water in the chamber starts rising.
Walking along the quay, the several docked ships are all in ruins. You swear you saw a candle light in a distant cabin.
A building near the coast crumbled on the paved street. The team is forced to board one of the decaying ship to circumvent the obstacle.
"The wood below the team's feet creaks dangerously as they advance through the docks."
"A ship sailing far from your position sounds its horns. It's unlikely they saw the expedition… right?"
A feral monkey rushes at the team, armed with a dull knife. Suddenly, a huge tentacle emerges from the dark sea and drags it below. This is a dangerous place…
Two flying devices spot the team; one immediately flies off.
He flips a switch and charges toward the adventurers.
A nearby patrol shifts its focus toward the team.
The first wave reaches the team and attacks with full force.
Another wave prepares to halt the advance.
A massive ship hovers overhead, as ground units leap several meters to the ground.
More ships approach, accompanied by ground support.
Two unknown devices on the side of the door are armed.
Two devices, identical to the ones encountered before, are activated.
The expedition spotted a massive, pale blue structure at the edge of the Barren Wastelands. After their report, a team is assigned to investigate.
With its source of power irreversibly compromised, the G.C.S.S. deactivates.
As they approach, it becomes clear the structure is of artificial origin.
With the whole Celestial Army at your heels, the team manage to climb onto the structure.
"Inside, the structure is even more alien: vast, empty spaces with ceilings soaring tens of meters high and architecture unlike anything they've ever seen."
In front, an imposing metal door blocks the path.
Behind the door is a large round room, with no other exits in sight.
In the center, a lone lever is present. When pulled, it lifts the team to the upper levels.
A small atrium lies ahead, with a door similar to the one they forced open earlier.
A long corridor leads to a round room filled with switches and levers.
In the center of the room, a towering humanoid rises from the command chair.
"Cracks begin to form on the structure's ceiling, suggesting the triggering of some safety mechanism."
As the room begins to collapse, someone pulls a lever on the right wall. In an instant, the team is teleported to high ground miles away, where they watch the building crumble from a safe distance.
Beneath the structure, hundreds of thousands of celestial soldiers stand ready in the distance.
Suddenly, the enemy ranks stir, metal clattering as they advance toward your position!
The expedition hurries across the barren landscape, skipping through the ever present banshee burrows.
As the celestial structure looms closer, the team shivers, awestruck by its immense size.
Chased by the entire celestial army, the team sharply veers into a narrow passage, hoping to delay the advance.
After a few minutes of running, the metallic clatter of the celestial horde fades a little, and the team spots the exit of the passage.
The expedition is now no more than a minute away from the building.
Several ropes hang from a metal platform above. The horde is closing in.
"[Darkness: %d%%] - There's plenty of light, and Adventurers can explore safely."
[Darkness: %d%%] - It might be a bit harder to hit enemies and dodge attacks and traps.
[Darkness: %d%%] - It will be difficult to hit enemies and dodge attacks and traps.
[Darkness: %d%%] - It will be very hard to hit enemies and dodge attacks and traps.
[Darkness: %d%%] - It will be almost impossible to hit enemies and dodge attacks and traps.
"A small Sha'huri group, likely standing guard to the sacred site, spots the team."
The ancient defense system activates once again, and warriors emerge from the sand. They look way more threatening than the ones you have met before.
Another wave of statues emerges from the sand, still gaining consistency at the time they first strike you.
The relentless stream of sentient sand keeps coming without a break.

"In the middle of the corridor, a huge figure is standing guard. It is unlike any Sha'huri warrior you have seen before: height reaching almost four meters, wielding four swords, one for each of its hands."

In the chamber, right at the center, a creature of unfathomable origin is standing perfectly still. It is unlike anything the team has seen before, inspiring deep rooted awe and overwhelming terror at the same time. When its eye opens, everyone present feels like their very soul was being peered into.

"After days of travels to the far East region of the Sha'huri desert, the colossal silhouette of a pyramid emerges from the horizon. Despite the current events its condition seems pristine, its apex still glistening with a golden sheen."
The adventurers navigate through the dunes, their boots sinking into the warm sand. Slowly, the pyramid is getting closer.
"Together, the adventurers push the door with all their strength. However, it doesn't seem to move. [Global Constitution required: 200]"
Together, the adventurers push the door with all their strength. Slowly, it opens wide to reveal a single, inner chamber.

Cracks starts forming on the alien being surface, as its eye look around frantically, almost scared. Suddenly, it explodes in a thousand pieces, leaving almost no trace. Almost, because on the ground lies a strange trinket…
The rhythmic crunch of footsteps harmonizes with the desert winds, as the expedition starts to make out the intricate block pattern that makes up the building.
The sound of blaring trumpets is heard in the distance, and the sand starts twisting below your feet. This is unlikely to be a good sign.
"Sha'huri deterrent system activated, threat level: EXTINCTION."
The trumpet sound finally stop, and the sand is once again at rest.
After some more minutes, the team is getting close to the pyramid. As they advance, the immense size of the construction becomes more apparent.
The expedition finally reaches the pyramid base. There is no door, just a wide opening on one of the sides that leads to a long corridor. Light is coming from ardent torches that lines the two walls.
The team walks deeper into the corridor that seems to never end, being thankful for the torches that make the travel less frightening.
A giant stone door blocks the path of the expedition. It is sealed shut, and bears the symbol of a triangle with an open eye inscribed inside.
%s attacked %s, but it was dodged. Dodge chance was %s%%
"%s attacked %s, but it can't reach flying targets"
There is a sound of a branch cracking. The team turns around.
Few meters ahead, from the bushes, a pair of eyes are watching the expedition.
Something was here before you, and has no intention to leave.
A low pitched growl echoes in the air.
You notice a movement behind the trees.
"The party sets foot in the forest just outside the guild's camp. Once a magical place where kids used to play, you feel the corruption tendrils are starting to reach these trees."
"A piercing scream echoes through the trees. It's rapidly getting closer…"
Among the sparse trees, an enraged spirit stands before you. \"Why did you do it…\" — the wind whispers.
"The group approaches an old fountain, covered in moss but otherwise perfectly functioning. After drinking its water, all wounds instantly disappear. Adventurers' HP are fully restored."

"The team finds a small fairy, trapped in a hunter's net and screaming at the top of her lungs. When they free her, she performs a quick spell and disappears into the crowns of the trees. Adventurers' Mana has been filled."
A large pitfall setup by hunters, concealed by a patch of leaves, lies in front of the team.
The team makes its way into a forest clearing, bathed in dim sunlight and surrounded by ancient trees.
There is a narrow forest path ahead, enclosed by towering trees.
"This area is engulfed by an abundance of high trees and untamed wilderness. It's very hard to see the sky above."
Blooming wildflowers are scattered everywhere, along with a few trees. Would have been a nice place for a camping trip in better times.
The trees make space for a narrow forest path, now muddy and overgrown with shrubs.
"Dead hands grasp the ground below the team's feet, struggling to reach the surface."
Right in front of you, something notices your presence. It instantly attacks.
Surprised by an unbearable stench, the team turns around to discover the enemies following them.
Something stands up from the burning pile of bodies, refusing to stay dead.
Without notice, the wind briefly opens up the smoke barrier, revealing the group to a hostile presence.

"The smell of the burning graves permeates the air, raising a thick smoke curtain that is hard to penetrate. The team advances carefully through the edge of the thousand years battlefield, unable to imagine how the corruption could have twisted the Sha'huri and Imperial remains that were left behind."
"The Will o' Wisp thanks you for freeing it from its mortal body. [Will o' Wisps slain: %d/200]"
"A Will o' Wisp descends from the sky. Unlike the others, he doesn't seem hostile. It offers an Orb of Ectoplasm as a gift and departs without a word."
"A cable holding an Imperial's explosive trap is stepped on."
"The team finds themselves on a hidden Sha'huri seal, covered by the ashes. It lightens up, and horrible visions flood the adventurers minds."
The adventurers cover their mouths as they pass a pile of burning remains.
The team enters a frugal encampment, now deserted, with plates still full of food near an extinguished campfire.
The sun, high in the sky, is barely visible though the tick fog.
"The ground is scattered by Sha'huri remains, displaying the kind of wounds that no weapon made by men could inflict."
In the distance, an army of undead is marching in casual directions.
After a long fight, the team realizes they are not going to win and run from the fight. [Fights end after 400 cumulative turns!]
The team notices a pungent smell in the air. Not long after, it discovers why.
There are footsteps in the snow. The trail ends soon to a group of enemies.
Behind a nearby rock, enemies were waiting for you.
Something was perfectly camouflaged in the white snow. It attacks the expedition as soon as they approach.
From a nearby cave opening, a group of enemies emerges to attack the team.

"The team begins the climb of the mountain range known as the Frostbite Peaks, well aware that it's freezing temperature and steep mountain passes are not the greatest danger: these mountains are said to be inhabited by trolls, a primitive humanoid species gifted with inhuman physical capabilities."
The wind gets suddenly colder. A blizzard descends upon the mountains, greatly reducing visibility and increasing the threat of freezing.
Behind a nearby rock lies a winterwood crate with a huge iron lock. It must be a Troll storage of sorts. With a Dexterity of %s, %s tries to pick the lock. It has a %s%% proability of success.
A pressure plate, hidden by snow, makes the ice crack below the teams feet. Soon enough, everyone will be submerged in freezing water.
A narrow passage forces the expedition to form a line and hug the mountain, being extremely careful as to not fall in the chasm below.
Even with the heaviest equipment, the ice cold climate makes every step harder than the previous.
The expedition stops for a break and lights a fire in a shallow caves opening.
In the distance, a magic pillar going all the way to the sky is visible. You must severe the link as soon as possible.
The team discovers a frozen pile of bodies, perfectly preserved from the cold. Bite marks and sings of blunt force trauma indicate that cold was unlikely the cause of death.
"Climbing gear is left suspended on the mountain side, covering it almost entirely. It has to be from the imperial army's passage."
There is imperial equipment scattered all over an extinguished campfire. It must be recent.
Adventurers are healed %s%% missing HP by %s
A sharp, whistling sound approaches at lightning speed.
"Turning a corner, menacing figures notice the team's presence, and suddenly attack."
Behind the team, enemies try a surprise attack.
Quick, unintelligible words are uttered nearby just before the team is attacked
A nearby wooden door is obliterated by an overwhelming power. From the dark room beyond, enemies surge toward the team.

The massive doors of the City of Larox, an ancient underground civilization lost for millennia, loom before the wary expedition. In the distance, a colossal artifact hums with seemingly random vibrations, reconfiguring itself in the blink of an eye. Using a sewer passage leading outside, the team slips past the marble walls undetected.

"In the distance, the Nexus shifts rapidly, forming shapes that defy human understanding. It emits a pulsating light before settling into a new, enigmatic configuration. Magic Damage amplification is now %d%%"
From the feet of one of the team members, light begins to reveal the radial symmetry of a magic seal. A fraction of second later, a defensive spell is triggered.

The air grows intensely dry. In the distance, the massive artifact begins to pulsate with increasing intensity. Along the sides of the street, obsidian walls spring up in an instant, shielding the civilian buildings.

"An old man pulls the team aside. He praises your actions on the surface and, unlike the haughty members of the council, expresses genuine hope that you succeed in reaching the lower caverns. He uncorks a vial with a dark liquid. Adventurers' HP are fully restored, harmful effects are cleansed."
From a nearby house, its walls adorned with arcane symbols, faint whispers in an ancient language can be heard.
Two tall empty armors, animated by a blue light, stand guard to a nearby street.
In the distance, the Nexus emits a strong shockwave, and reconfigures itself once more.
A procession of robed individuals walks through a large street ahead. The team proceeds with extreme caution.
On a nearby doorstep, five candles around a burnt, red incision suggest some kind of ritual recently took place.
A skeleton lies suspended below a second floor window. What kind of civilized society allows this?
Several crystals emerging from the ground, a natural occurrence in these caverns, vibrate in the same frequency of the Nexus.
Candles in a nearby house are immediately put off as the team approaches.
A loud shout echoes in the distance, swiftly followed by a lightning in the same spot.
High above, a small, misshapen flying creature with a reddish hue soars through the air, clutching a piece of furniture.
A crowd of enraged citizen fills the courtyard. They attack you.
Another wave comes at you with bloodshot eyes.
Another group engages. They want your heads.
A group of guards is wandering the corridors aimlessly. As soon as they see you, they engage the fight.
Another team of sentinels attacks you.
The guests, probably struck by the corruption during the cursed meal, are still sitting at the table.
A team of palace guards is roaming before the door.
An inhumane scream comes from above the opened door, behind the team. Looking up, a hideous creature, still dressed in royal insignia, leaps down from the ceiling.

In the center of the Golden City, a dilapidated Imperial Palace overlooks the surrounding area. While this expedition is a significant deviation from your voyage to the north, it is your duty to try to rescue the Emperor of a friendly nation. Therefore, King Roderic gave your guild the order to do everything you can to bring His Majesty to safety.
The team reaches the entrance of the huge courtyard. The Eye above is looking interested.
Looking at the table, they notice the food is black with mold: it must have lied there for weeks.
At the end of the room, an open door leads to a short corridor. It leads to a single door, at its end.
The door bears the seal of the Clovis family. It is closed, but unlocked.
"The open door reveals the Emperor's Throne Room. It has been thrashed, without a single furniture being intact or in it's supposed place."
The golden throne, still in its place, is empty.
With the Emperor finally at rest, the team leaves the forsaken palace to report the events to the King.
Marble statues with golden detail stand all over the perimeter, an immortal testament of the opulence of this court.
In the middle of the courtyard an adorned fountain, now out of function, acts as the central decoration.
At the end of the courtyard, a wide granite staircase leads up to the entrance of the Palace.
One side of the door is halfway open. The expedition enters the palace.
On the ground, a red carpet with golden edges extends all the way through the intertwined corridors.
The team advances through rows of marble statues, recognizing at least a couple renowned generals.
At the end of the corridor, the team finds a locked door, intricately decorated but easy to break down.
The adventurers find themselves in a large dining room, with a long laden table.
A wave of mutated horrors surges down the road.
It crushes the old man in an instant and turn toward the adventurers.
They direct their attention at the intruders.
"The manor's security force descends from all directions."
Instantly, they sprint down to attack.
They raise from their seats and attack.

The machine lights up, and the molten core reveals a passage to a desolate land, with a sky darkened by ominous clouds. The expedition steps through and arrives at the edge of a dilapidated village, marked by strange, unfamiliar architecture.
Rag-clad villagers glance at the newcomers and wave them away in fear. Moments later, they all retreat inside their homes.
The gates of a grand manor draw near. On the front steps, a group of disfigured mutants stands guard.
"Inside, the manor's main hall is decrepit. Piles of broken furniture are stacked against one wall."
On the wide marble staircase, more writhing masses of flesh await.
A long corridor stretches above the stairs. The throne room must be close.
"At the corridor's end stands a massive cracked door, half-open."
Beyond the door, the Royal Council sits around a table, strewn with rotten food and shattered bottles.
A monstrous figure wearing a rusted crown, once a man, now something else, calls for the guards. No one answers.
The council members lie on the ground, with the mysterious technology already repairing their wounds. The adventurers start their travel back to the portal.
An old man emerges from one of the crumbling houses. He warns that others will come soon, then begins recounting the story of his world: a utopia turned nightmare.
He speaks of the discovery of immortality, and of the mental decay triggered by the repeated return of the Black Serpent.
Of the discovery of the Panacea, able to stop the decline and allowing the ruling class to cling to power indefinitely.
And of the lie begotten by their fear, which created a demented government guided by madness, focused on creating the most advanced forms of repression disregarding all ethics.
From behind a building, a large monster emerges along with its following.
A red castle, enveloped by lightnings, looms at the horizon.
The adventurers continue down winding country roads, surrounded by barren fields.
The march is long and uneventful, until they spot something far away.
From beyond the thick wall of leaves, enemies charge at the team.
Behind the team, enemies are quickly approaching.
A group of enemies emerges from the dark entrance of a nearby pyramid.
The team is ambushed by enemies, who were waiting on the tall trees.
As they round a bend in the winding stone path, the team is confronted by a group of enemies.
